label: Matt 4:1
text: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.

label: Matt 4:2
text: When he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was hungry afterward.

label: Matt 4:3
text: The tempter came and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.”

label: Matt 4:4
text: But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.’”

label: Matt 4:5
text: Then the devil took him into the holy city. He set him on the pinnacle of the temple,

label: Matt 4:6
text: and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down, for it is written, ‘He will put his angels in charge of you.’ and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, so that you don’t dash your foot against a stone.’”

label: Matt 4:7
text: Jesus said to him, “Again, it is written, ‘You shall not test the Lord, your God.’”

label: Matt 4:8
text: Again, the devil took him to an exceedingly high mountain, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory.

label: Matt 4:9
text: He said to him, “I will give you all of these things, if you will fall down and worship me.”

label: Matt 4:10
text: Then Jesus said to him, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’”

label: Matt 4:11
text: Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and served him.

label: Matt 4:12
text: Now when Jesus heard that John was delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee.

label: Matt 4:13
text: Leaving Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,

label: Matt 4:14
text: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,

label: Matt 4:15
text: “The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,

label: Matt 4:16
text: the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, to those who sat in the region and shadow of death, to them light has dawned.”

label: Matt 4:17
text: From that time, Jesus began to preach, and to say, “Repent! For the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.”

label: Matt 4:18
text: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.

label: Matt 4:19
text: He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”

label: Matt 4:20
text: They immediately left their nets and followed him.

label: Matt 4:21
text: Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them.

label: Matt 4:22
text: They immediately left the boat and their father, and followed him.

label: Matt 4:23
text: Jesus went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

label: Matt 4:24
text: The report about him went out into all Syria. They brought to him all who were sick, afflicted with various diseases and torments, possessed with demons, epileptics, and paralytics; and he healed them.

label: Matt 4:25
text: Great multitudes from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and from beyond the Jordan followed him.

label: Wikipedia: Capernaum
title: Capernaum
excerpt: Archaeological evidence demonstrates that the town was established in the 2nd century BC during the Hasmonean period, when several fishing villages sprang up around the lake.

label: Wikipedia: Capernaum (small finds)
title: Capernaum (small finds)
excerpt: Fish hooks, weights for fish nets, striker pins, weaving bobbins, and basalt mills for milling grain and pressing olives were also found.

label: Wikipedia: Capernaum (the synagogue)
title: Capernaum (the synagogue)
excerpt: The synagogue appears to have been built around the 4th or 5th century. Beneath the foundation of this synagogue lies another foundation made of basalt, and Loffreda suggests that this is the foundation of a synagogue from the 1st century, perhaps the one mentioned in the Gospels.

label: Wikipedia: Capernaum (house of Peter)
title: Capernaum (house of Peter)
excerpt: The excavators concluded that one house in the village was venerated as the house of Peter the fisherman as early as the mid-1st century, with two churches having been constructed over it.

label: Wikipedia: Capernaum (identification doubted)
title: Capernaum (identification doubted)
excerpt: In particular, where excavators had claimed to find graffiti including the name of Peter, others have found very little legible writing.

label: Wikipedia: Sea of Galilee Boat
title: Sea of Galilee Boat
excerpt: The Ancient Galilee Boat, also known as the Jesus Boat, is an ancient fishing boat from the 1st century AD, discovered in 1986 on the north-west shore of the Sea of Galilee in Israel.

label: Wikipedia: Sea of Galilee Boat (no link to Jesus)
title: Sea of Galilee Boat (no link to Jesus)
excerpt: Other than the dating, there is no evidence connecting the boat to Jesus or his disciples.

label: Wikipedia: Magdala (fishing gear)
title: Magdala (fishing gear)
excerpt: Artifacts discovered in the excavations of the 1970s include a needle and lead weights for repairing and holding down fishing nets, and numerous coins.

label: Wikipedia: Magdala (Tarichaea disputed)
title: Magdala (Tarichaea disputed)
excerpt: derived from the Greek Τάριχος or tarichos, meaning 'fish preserved by salting or drying'

label: Wikipedia: Migdal Synagogue
title: Migdal Synagogue
excerpt: The first synagogue was discovered in 2009 during a salvage dig conducted by Dr. Dina Avshalom-Gorni of the Israel Antiquities Authority at the location of a new hotel at Migdal Beach, the site of ancient Magdala.

label: Wikipedia: Migdal Synagogue (scarcity)
title: Migdal Synagogue (scarcity)
excerpt: The Migdal site is just one of seven synagogues known to date back to the Second Temple period

label: Wikipedia: Trumpeting Place inscription
title: Trumpeting Place inscription
excerpt: The Trumpeting Place inscription is an inscribed stone from the 1st century CE discovered in 1968 by Benjamin Mazar in his early excavations of the southern wall of the Temple Mount.

label: Wikipedia: Herod Antipas
title: Herod Antipas
excerpt: Augustus confirmed the testament of the dead king by making Antipas tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, a region he ruled for 42 years.

label: Wikipedia: Herod Antipas (coins)
title: Herod Antipas (coins)
excerpt: His coins carried no images, which would have violated Jewish prescriptions against idolatry.

label: Wikipedia: John the Baptist (Josephus)

label: Wikipedia: Judaean Desert (fortresses)

label: Wikipedia: Monastery of the Temptation
title: Monastery of the Temptation
excerpt: It was built on the slopes of the Mount of Temptation 350 meters above sea level, situated along a cliff overlooking the city of Jericho and the Jordan Valley.

label: Wikipedia: Monastery of the Temptation (tradition)

excerpt: Its most ancient structures date back to the 6th century, having been built above the cave traditionally said to be that where Jesus spent forty days and forty nights fasting and meditating while he was tempted by Satan.

label: Wikipedia: Decapolis
title: Decapolis
excerpt: Under Roman rule, the cities of the Decapolis were not included in the territory of the Herodian kingdom, its successor states of the Herodian tetrarchy, or the Roman province of Judea.

label: Wikipedia: Decapolis (nature of the league)

excerpt: The Decapolis was probably never an official political or economic union; most likely it signified the collection of city-states which enjoyed special autonomy during early Roman rule.
